why.B1.1: Single S2 and systolic ejection murmur, along with enlarged cardiac silhouette and increased pulmonary vasculature, are highly suggestive of Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
why.B2.1: Ventricular Septal Defect is a possible cause, given the presence of a systolic ejection murmur and enlarged cardiac silhouette, but it is less specific than Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
why.B3.2: Tricuspid Atresia is a possibility, but the evidence is not as strong as for Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome, and the presence of a single S2 and systolic ejection murmur can be seen in other conditions
why.B4.2: Truncus Arteriosus could be a consideration due to the common arterial trunk, but the findings are not as typical as those for Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
why.B5.1: Respiratory Infection is unlikely, as the cardiac auscultation and chest imaging findings suggest a cardiac pathology rather than a non-cardiac cause
